1.why: Every MFA route goes through authenticated(), which resolves the account solely from the session's userId, and hasForeignIdentity() rejects any client-supplied userId/accountId/ownerId.

2.why: Codes are checked only against per-session, single-use, expiring challenge objects (identity, enrollment, mfaChallenge) and only one account exists, so no code can be used for any other user.

3.why: /api/mfa/confirm merely sets session.enrollment = null and never deletes or rotates the session, so the existing authenticated session (and any prior ones) keeps working after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The OTP secret is stored AES-GCM-encrypted via encryptSecret() and recovery codes are stored as salted SHA-256 hashes via storeRecoveryCodes(), never in plain text.

5.why: Session IDs, CSRF tokens, TOTP secrets, and recovery codes are all generated with crypto.getRandomValues, a CSPRNG.

6.why: The session cookie is set HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict and the client keeps secrets and codes only in in-memory JS variables, with no localStorage/sessionStorage usage.

7.why: The server validates all input with isEmail/isPhone/isOtp/isRecovery/isSecret allow-regex checks plus JSON shape and 4KB body-size limits.

8.why: All dynamic values (secret, label, codes, messages) are rendered via textContent in escText(), and CSP restricts script/style execution to per-response nonces.

9.why: allowedRedirect() permits only undefined, "/", or "/mfa", rejecting any external redirect target.

10.why: securityHeaders() sets CSP (including frame-ancestors 'none'), HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY on every response.

11.why: cookie() emits the mfa_session cookie with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: The client-side log() function writes the authenticator secret, test OTPs, and recovery codes to console and a visible Logs panel, so secrets are not kept out of logs, although URLs are clean, errors are generic, and no stack traces are shown.

13.why: Every challenge is marked used on success and expires after CHALLENGE_MS (5 minutes), and recovery codes are permanently consumed on use.

14.why: failed() locks the relevant record for LOCK_MS (10 minutes) after 5 failures, enforced on identity checks, enrollment, MFA challenges, and the recovery guard.

15.why: rotateAuthenticated() deletes the pending session and issues a fresh ID upon authentication, sessions enforce 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute expiry, and /api/logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
